transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 16:00 PT | Duration: ~58 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood Legal/SE), Susan Patel (Aperture Proc), David Liang (Aperture Head Data & AI), Karen O'Neill (Aperture Counsel), Mark Rivera (Infra), Anita Bose (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, appreciate the procurement and legal folks joining. The goal today is basically vendor gating — make sure we have the MSA/DPA covers, SLA language and a pricing path you can take to your pricing committee. We'll walk through the items, hear your required gating criteria, and surface any blockers.
[00:23] Susan: Hi Alex, thanks. Just to flag, procurement needs PO terms, invoice frequency, and whether we need annual or monthly commitments. We'll also need pricing ceilings for budget committee.
[00:38] David: And from Data & AI side, we need clarity on private deployment options, dedicated capacity guarantees, and what data resides in Redwood control plane vs our VPC.
[00:52] Karen: Legal — our main asks are breach notification windows, subprocessor disclosures, data deletion guarantees, and indemnity caps. We also have a vendor questionnaire we'll push to you.
[01:10] Priya: Great—I'll jump in on technical parts. For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and SLO-backed latency targets. For hosted, it's simpler usage pricing but less isolation.
[01:25] Mark: Can you confirm whether Dedicated includes a private control plane or is it always a hosted control plane with network peering?
[01:33] Miguel: Quick clar — sometimes the names vary; Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option with customer-managed control plane, Dedicated is reserved capacity in our environment but with stronger isolation. We can send a diagram.
[01:48] Karen: We need that architecture diagram for the vendor questionnaire — clearly annotated on where keys live.
[02:00] Anita: Security note — we must see KMS/HSM integration options and whether customer keys are supported end-to-end. Also will need SOC2 report and penetration test cadence.
[02:18] Alex: Miguel has the SOC2 link and sub-processor list; we'll attach those to the redlined MSA.
[02:26] Miguel: I'll also include our standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) — note on HSM we support customer-managed HSM via partner integrations, but I'll clarify exact flows.
[02:40] Susan: On pricing, we asked for committed spend. The spending committee wants a 12-month committed look and also a 6-month option. Can you provide cost per token and effective unit price with caching/batching assumptions?
[02:55] Priya: Yes, we'll produce scenarios. Important caveat: unit token pricing often depends on model size and quantization, and Dedicated has a different effective cost due to reserved capacity amortization. We'll show committed discounts and burst options.
[03:12] David: Any penalties or price escalation clauses we should expect in the MSA?
[03:18] Alex: Our standard MSA has an annual price escalation clause tied to CPI with a cap — but we're flexible in enterprise contracts; we can propose a fixed escalation cap for Aperture if that helps procurement signoff.
[03:30] Karen: On breach notification, our security policy requires notice within 72 hours of discovery. How does Redwood typically handle that?
[03:39] Miguel: Standard language we provide is 72 hours for notifying a material breach affecting customer data; we can keep that. We usually also offer cooperation commitments for incident response and a point of contact.
[03:51] Anita: Will that include forensic logs retention and sharing of redacted logs? We need at least 90 days of audit log availability for investigations.
[04:03] Miguel: We retain audit logs per contract; the DPA can specify 90 days or longer. We'll propose 180 days as standard for enterprise and flag options.
[04:15] Susan: Procurement question: do you accept a PO and net-30? Any exceptions?
[04:21] Alex: Yes we accept PO and net-30 by default; for larger enterprise contracts we can negotiate net-45 or net-60 but usually require a signed MSA and sometimes require initial payment or deposit depending on committed spend.
[04:34] Mark: Network question — for VPC connectors, is traffic tunneled through a managed connector or do you support private link equivalents?
[04:41] Priya: We support multiple routing options; for private we can do direct peering or dedicated private links depending on cloud provider. We'll include a network options doc.
[04:52] David: On data residency, our clinical data must remain in the EU for certain tenants. Does Redwood support region-restricted deployments?
[04:59] Miguel: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted we can provision model runtime in specific regions; for Private you can fully locate the control plane. We'll capture data residency controls in the DPA.
[05:12] Karen: There's always the indemnity conversation — Aperture's policy tries to limit indemnities to breaches caused by vendor negligence and caps to X times fees; what's Redwood's position?
[05:23] Alex: Our baseline is mutual indemnity with a cap tied to 12 months of fees, but we can discuss sliding caps for higher tiers. We'll flag that in the redline.
[05:35] Susan: Timing wise, procurement needs pricing approval by the 30th to make the August exec committee. Can Redwood meet that?
[05:43] Alex: Yes — we're targeting to have pricing scenarios and redlines in the next 48–72 hours.
[05:50] [06:00] Priya: Also want to surface an operational note — for P95 latency SLOs we typically commit to 250–400ms depending on model and prompt length; Dedicated with pinned VMs will give you the tightest P95. We'll include example SLO numbers.
[06:20] David: Would you include the fallback policy in the SLA? E.g., if a model variant is unavailable we want automatic fallback to a compatible variant with a known degradation profile.
[06:29] Priya: Yes that is part of our smart routing — we'll document fallback tiers and expected latency/quality tradeoffs.
[06:40] Karen: Contract clause question about data deletion — we require deletion confirmation within 30 days of contract termination for customer data and logs. Can that be honored?
[06:50] Miguel: We can commit to deletion of customer data and provide certificates of deletion; logs that are needed for security may be retained in anonymized form per the DPA, but we'll include an explicit timeline — 30 days for primary data, 90 days for backup rotation window by default, but we can negotiate.
[07:05] Anita: Also encryption at rest — is it customer-controlled keys for model state and KV cache?
[07:12] Priya: For KV cache and runtime artifacts, encryption at rest is standard; customer-managed keys are supported for dedicated/private setups. We'll clarify which artifacts can be key-controlled.
[07:22] Susan: About the vendor questionnaire — we'll send it overnight. Expect about 20 items prioritized. If you can get back within 48 hours that would be great.
[07:33] Alex: We'll commit to 48 hours for the high priority ones.
[07:38] [08:00] Karen: A few specific redline asks: carveouts around customer-supplied data, tighter SLA credits, and an audit right clause limited to scope and frequency. We'll annotate the vendor questionnaire with examples.
[08:14] Miguel: For audit rights we typically do a combination: periodic SOC2 report plus one on-site audit per year with notice, or virtual audit. We can narrow scope to data processing activities only.
[08:28] David: For Dedicated cost modeling, what's the expected burn for a 4x A100 equivalent pool? Rough estimates for budgeting?
[08:37] Priya: We'll provide price per hour per GPU and amortized monthly cost with utilization assumptions. The committed model will assume a 70% utilization baseline; burst credits allow headroom.
[08:48] Susan: Procurement needs sample invoice and a sample SOW format for services — who do we send SOW templates to?
[08:54] Alex: Send to me, I'll loop in ops; we have a standard SOW template we can adapt for pilots and professional services.
[09:02] Mark: On monitoring — do we provide token-level cost breakup to integrate into FinOps dashboards?
[09:09] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and per-route breakdowns, exportable via CSV or API. We'll include an example export and the schema.
[09:22] Karen: Any blockers on the redlined MSA? We will push a vendor questionnaire and expect to receive Redwood's redline and artifacts for legal review.
[09:30] Miguel: No blockers; we'll send the redlined MSA and DPA plus SOC2 link and sub-processor list by Friday.
[09:37] Susan: Great. If those are in hand, procurement can expedite the pricing approval by 2025-07-30.
[09:45] Alex: Perfect — recap: Redwood action items are redline MSA/DPA, sub-processor list, SOC2 link, dedicated pricing scenarios, and network architecture diagram. Aperture action items are vendor questionnaire and internal decision timeline.
[09:58] David: Quick practical note — we may ask for a short pilot with a capped budget to validate latency and quality before committing. How do pilots usually get billed?
[10:08] Priya: Pilots can be usage billed or small committed blocks; for pilots we often do a time-boxed credit or trial account with support. We'll put options in the pricing worksheet.
[10:19] Karen: One small point on export controls — our legal team may need confirmation that models and outputs don't have restrictions; likely fine, but we'll flag it in the questionnaire.
[10:30] Miguel: We'll provide a short note on model provenance and licensing for each model we propose.
[10:38] [11:00] Susan: Ok, timeline: vendor questionnaire out today, Redwood artifacts by Friday, procurement signoff target 2025-07-30, gating call week of 2025-07-29. Does that align?
[11:15] Alex: Yes, we'll hit those dates. Anything else?
[11:20] Anita: Please ensure the KMS integration details include key rotation policies and whether Redwood will ever have access to plaintext keys. That's a hard requirement.
[11:32] Miguel: We'll specify that customer-managed keys remain under customer control — Redwood won't have plaintext access; we'll detail rotation and split-key if applicable.
[11:44] David: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[11:48] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Follow-up meeting to be scheduled after legal review.
[11:56] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: Some spoken acronyms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KMS sometimes shown as KMC), occasional speaker label mis-assignments. References to technical components: KV cache, Dedicated capacity, VPC, Private control plane, SOC 2, DPA, MSA, SOW, PO, KMS/HSM. References to competitor alternatives: Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock.

References shared during call: link:Redwood SOC2 report (sent post-meeting), link:Dedicated pricing worksheet (Priya to share), doc:Network-architecture-diagram (Priya), file:Vendor-questionnaire (Aperture to send).
